clue.text: Formal request for something to put on

definitions.meaning: a written request, as for a job or a licence
an ointment or lotion is put on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a written submission asking for something and a cream or paint spread on a surface.

clue.text: Small coin isn't common but it's pe colourful

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Small coin isn't common but it's pe colourful': P (small coin) + AINT (isn't, non-standard) gives the letters, but 'pe' is garbled OCR and no word left defines the answer as a noun or verb; the definition cannot be recovered.
annotationWithheld.clue: Small coin isn't common but it's pe colourful

clue.text: Roped in girl over a dictionary

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: lass is a common word for a girl
OED, the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: Someone has been dragooned into the job by a girl, with a dictionary somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roped in' reads as persuaded to join, but here it is caught with a rope. 'over' places LASS above OED in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch an animal with a looped rope, so lassoed means roped.

clue.text: Lyrical as Beethoven's Ninth Symphony

definitions.meaning: its nickname is the ... Symphony, as its finale sets the Ode to Joy for chorus

explanation.definitionFit: Music for voices is choir music, and Beethoven's Ninth is nicknamed for its sung finale.

clue.text: Its contents are destined to go to pot

definitions.text: Its contents are destined to go to pot

parts.words: Its contents are destined to go to pot
parts.note: a box of dried leaves which will end up brewed in a teapot, not ruined

explanation.surface: Something whose contents are bound to be wasted or ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wooden box shipping tea, whose leaves end up in the teapot.

clue.text: Measure a Roman emperor takes in Shakespearean tragedy

indicators.note: the emperor's name swallows the measure, holding it inside

parts.note: Otho reigned briefly in AD 69, the year of four emperors
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor sits through a performance of a Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an emperor watching a play; 'takes in' is a container signal, not seeing a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about the jealous Moor of Venice is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Consuming interest-before work?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
an occupation is one's work or job

explanation.surface: Asks whether a consuming interest might come before the day job.
explanation.definitionFit: An absorbing concern that fills the mind is an obsession, a consuming interest.

clue.text: To whom dope substance should be familiar

definitions.text: To whom dope substance should be familiar

parts.note: slang for a drug
the gist is the substance or essence of something

explanation.surface: A question of who ought to know all about a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist, who deals in medicines and so should know any drug.

clue.text: Health threat to bear in mind

definitions.text: Health threat to bear in mind

parts.words: Health threat to bear in mind
parts.note: reads as a warning to remember, but means a danger to mental health that must be borne in the mind, a ground for divorce

explanation.surface: A health risk the reader is urged to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological abuse, cited as grounds for divorce, endured in the mind and damaging to mental wellbeing.

clue.text: Complains bitterly about cranes, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to rail is to protest angrily
cranes run along tracks; also, the birds so named are kin to cranes

explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to rant, and overhead cranes travel on metal tracks of the same name.

clue.text: Indicted at Balaclava?

definitions.meaning: formally accused, especially of a military offence
the Charge of the Light Brigade took place at Balaclava in the Crimean War

explanation.definitionFit: An accused soldier is put on report, and the Light Brigade at Balaclava were literally charging.

clue.text: Mashed potatoes at hospital for a healer

indicators.note: mashed vegetables are crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital serves mashed potatoes to a practitioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed' is the anagram signal on the vegetables; 'at' and 'for a' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles is a kind of healer.

clue.text: Dramatic entertainment that should be illuminating

definitions.text: Dramatic entertainment that should be illuminating

parts.words: Dramatic entertainment that should be illuminating
parts.note: a stage genre whose first word, read as brightness, suggests it ought to shed illumination

explanation.surface: A theatre piece that is supposed to be enlightening.
explanation.definitionFit: A play of a gentle humorous kind, a genre of the stage.

clue.text: See 13
Suitable entrance to the City of London for 6?

definitions.text: Suitable entrance to the City of London for 6?

parts.words: Suitable entrance to the City of London for 6?
parts.note: 6 down's hero is a North African, so the fitting way in for him is the London gate named after his people

explanation.surface: Which gateway into the City would suit a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is OTHELLO, the Moor of Venice; one of the old City of London wall gates bears that word.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the old gates in London's Roman wall, now a station and street in the City.

clue.text: Source of calories in a show, palace near Madrid

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Source of calories in a show, palace near Madrid': the answer is an anagram of CALORIES, but 'Source of' has no job (the anagram indicator is presumably 'in a show'), so the clue as held is likely misread and no source confirms the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Source of calories in a show, palace near Madrid

clue.text: Player with flat to change suit in

indicators.note: the letters are to alter their order

explanation.surface: Someone moving flat changes suit while inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges FLAT and SUIT together; 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute player is a musician, a player of an instrument.

clue.text: How hesitant actors are cued

parts.note: actors who dry are fed their lines by the prompter, so they are given lines in the manner of a prompt

explanation.surface: The way actors who falter are given their next line.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately, without delay, and also by means of a prompt.

clue.text: Faded around tea-time to become inactive

indicators.note: the word for faded goes round the time, enclosing it

parts.note: passe means past its best, faded
four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals, is traditional British teatime

explanation.surface: Something fading in the late afternoon until it goes still.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime in Britain is traditionally four o'clock, hence the Roman numeral; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Passive means accepting without acting, so inert, inactive.

clue.text: Perhaps his back trouble is improving

definitions.text: Perhaps his back trouble is improving

parts.words: Perhaps his back trouble is improving
parts.note: reads as a sore back mending, but a punter is one who backs horses, and getting well is also the word

explanation.surface: Someone's bad back is perhaps on the mend.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is one who bets, and improving health is getting well, the same word.

clue.text: Anyhow it's one with a republican status

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Somehow a place has republican standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic republic, a state with that status since independence from the USSR.

clue.text: Got stuck in

parts.note: reads as set to work with gusto, but means jammed tight

explanation.surface: Someone started work with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jammed fast into a gap is firmly lodged there.

clue.text: Banker with an attachment to us

parts.note: a tag is a label attached to something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank official keeps hold of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword shorthand for a river, which has banks; the Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something with banks, and this is the Iberian river reaching the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: A neat blue concoction not to be consumed

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tidy blue cocktail that should not be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food cannot be eaten, so it is not to be consumed.

clue.text: Commonplace as a false god with a hearty name

indicators.note: read as having something at its heart, so the name goes in the middle

parts.note: Baal was a Canaanite god, a false god in the Bible

explanation.surface: Something ordinary, compared to a false idol with a cheerful name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearty' puts N into the heart of BAAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite, lacking originality, so ordinary.

clue.text: Picking up in boating accident

indicators.note: a boating accident wrecks the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone collecting injuries in a boating mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain is to get or acquire, as does picking something up.

clue.text: Composition for players one over the eight

definitions.meaning: a piece of music written for a group of instrumentalists
eight plus one gives nine; in British slang one over the eight also means tipsy

explanation.definitionFit: A piece for nine musicians, nine being one more than eight.

clue.text: Strapping noblemen beaten up?

parts.note: peers wearing a belt of rank, read as aristocrats who have been thrashed

explanation.surface: Burly aristocrats who have been given a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls invested with a belt as a mark of rank, a term in heraldry and old usage.
